title: PBT all of it
body:
# Full-syntax PBT generators

Our PBTs ran against hand-written generators covering a curated subset of the
language — no modules, no `theorem`/`forall`, no invalid tiles, labeled tuples only
in a few positions. This replaces them with ppx-derived generators that reach **every**
constructor of the Menhir AST, and fixes everything that fell out.

One commit adds the generators, one commit per suite flips it over and fixes what it
finds, one commit deletes the old generators. Each migration commit is self-contained.

Two things that change across the board:

- **`size` changed meaning.** `arb_exp(50)` was a node budget; `arb_exp_full(5)` is
  depth fuel, halved per recursive step. Counts drop 10 000 → 1 000: full-syntax terms
  are far more expensive to build and evaluate. Wider per term, fewer terms.
- **Failures are real.** The generator only emits terms the printer and Menhir lexer
  round-trip, and `Canonicalize` absorbs genuine print aliases, so a failure means a gap.

---

### `Stop ExplicitNonlabel shrinkers from looping forever`

- `shrink_{exp,pat,typ}` returned `ExplicitNonlabel` *for* `ExplicitNonlabel` — a
  shrinker yielding its own input, so QCheck never terminates. Now `Iter.empty`.

### `Add ppx-derived full-syntax QCheck generators`

Derives `arb_exp_full` / `arb_typ_full` from the Menhir AST. Shaping needed to stay
inside what the lexer and printer can express:

- Identifiers, livelit names (`^name`), constructor names get `[@gen]` so they stay
  lexically valid.
- `Invalid*` payloads draw from a closed face-token set (`^o^`, `?_?`, …) — the junk
  tiles MakeTerm actually classifies as `Invalid`. Operator-shaped junk (`!!!`) molds
  as an infix with holes instead, so it's useless as an `Invalid` example.
- Lists capped at 0–3; the ppx default reaches ~10k and explodes recursive terms.
- `TupLabel` left sides restricted to `Label` / `ExplicitNonlabel` — the only forms
  that print and parse as `lab=e` / `_=e`.
- `UnknownType` only generates the printable `EmptyHole`; `Module` binders are
  `VarPat` only; `DynamicErrorHole`'s payload must parse as an error sexp.

Also:

- `ppx_minimal_idents` lets a suite ask for `x`/`y` instead of random letters, so
  generated programs actually bind things.
- Generators are memoized by fuel — building one eagerly expands to
  ~`positions^log2(n)` closures, and rebuilding per suite OOMs Node.
- `Conversion.Typ.of_core_type_provenance` raised on any provenance but
  `Internal`/`EmptyHole`, which crashed shrinking (it goes through `~rev`). Every
  provenance now maps to a printable form.
- Sort-specific renames: `ExplicitNonlabel` → `ExplicitNonlabel{,Pat,Type}`.

### `Migrate Test_Grammar PBT to the full-syntax generator`

- One-liner. Annotation map/unmap was already total.

### `Migrate Test_Elaboration PBT to the full-syntax generator`

- `case (()) | _ => [(let `a` = x in x)] end` — a quoted-label binder synthesizes
  `Label("a")`, which reached `Coverage.all_ctrs_of_type` and hit its
  "non-normalized type" `failwith`. A `Label` isn't a sum; it joins the non-sum forms.
- Bare `_` in pat sort is `ExplicitNonlabel` at the MakeTerm tip, but `PatternMatch`
  only knows `Wild`. Elaboration now emits `Wild` and keeps the mark.

### `Migrate Test_Statics_Properties PBTs to the full-syntax generator`

This suite asserts elaboration is a fixed point, so every fix is about idempotence.

- `x((?))` where `x` is an unknown builtin — dynamics raises `InvalidBuiltin` for
  anything outside `Builtins.forms_init`. Unknown names now elaborate to `Invalid`
  (Indet under `Transition`, same synthesized type). Not `Var`, which would resolve
  against an enclosing binding of the same name.
- `proof_of` quoted the *user* term while `elab_term` held the elaborated one, so
  re-elaboration produced a type that wasn't `fast_equal` to the recorded one — and
  broke the side condition on the `(ProofObject, ProofOf)` ascription rule. Both now
  quote `e_elab`.
- `FixF` wrapped its body in `Asc` unconditionally, adding a layer per pass. Now only
  when the ascription would change the body's type.
- Constructor patterns recomputed `elab_ty` even when already resolved, regressing it
  to `Some(None)` on the second pass.
- Test side: the elaborated program must be re-checked with `use_mode = None`.
  `use SInt in -?` elaborates to an `SInt` minus, which a `Some(Int)` pass rewrites
  back to `Int`. (`CachedStatics` already does this.)

### `Migrate Test_Evaluator_Properties PBTs to the full-syntax generator`

- `let y = y in y` → substitution produced `let y' = y' in y'`. The RHS isn't under
  the binder, so freshening a shadowing binder must not rewrite it.
- `fun x -> 1` with a `Sig` in the annotation slot — only *surface* ascriptions go
  through `desugar_sig`, so substitution met a `SigLet` pattern inside a type and hit
  a `failwith`. Signature names are field labels, not expression binders, so we
  recurse and leave them alone; statics also normalizes `Fun`'s annotation now.
- `fix x -> (theorem ? = y in x)` — `Theorem`/`Forall` step to Indet but their bodies
  still mention environment variables. Without `wrap_closure`, big-step left `x` free
  while small-step substituted.
- `forall x(x) -> x` — big-step alpha-renames the later binder, small-step doesn't.
  `Alphas.combine` is first-match, so duplicate binders need the *later* binders
  passed first to shadow correctly.
- `DynamicErrorHole((()))` — the `req_final` binder shadowed the outer term, so
  `wrap_closure` wrapped the child and dropped the hole.

### `Migrate Test_TextRoundtrip PBT to the full-syntax generator`

- One-liner. The print→parse→print fixed point already held.

### `Migrate Test_Menhir PBTs to the full-syntax generator`

The big one — Menhir↔MakeTerm equivalence is what full syntax exposes most.

**Menhir learns the syntax it was missing:** `theorem`, `forall`, `proof_object`,
`proof_of`, `Nat`/`SInt`, quoted labels in pat and typ position, invalid faces in every
sort, `module _ =` / `module ? =`, `hint <exp> test … end` (was string-literal only),
and `undef` → `undefined`.

Two restructurings:

- **`sumTerm` derives `typ`.** MakeTerm classifies *any* type in sum position —
  `TypVar` → `Variant`, else `BadEntry` — so `sumTerm` does too. Because it can then
  derive a leading-plus sum, `+ A + B` reduced to `Sum([BadEntry(Sum …)])` where
  MakeTerm has a flat sum; `splice_sumterm` flattens it back.
  Heads of *no-lead* sums (`Nil + Cons(Int, T)`, `HasInt(Int) + HasMore(...)`) get
  their own nonterminal, since an applied constructor isn't a `typ` and a general
  `sumTerm PLUS …` head would be swallowed by the leading-plus rules.
- **`typ` split into `typ`/`typ_inner`** so `...` sits looser than `->`, matching
  `Precedence`. `%prec` can't express it — `TUPLE_EXTENSION` also carries exp-level
  precedence. Function params gain a layer so ascription binds tighter than cons:
  `fun p : T :: q ->` is `ConsPat(AscPat(p,T), q)`, as MakeTerm reads it.

**Where the two parsers disagreed:**

- `undefined . ((`l`))` — Menhir erases parens, so the `.` field tip has to peel them
  or MakeTerm sees a field access and Menhir a `MultiHole`. Same for `=` tips.
- `{ o^o }` — MakeTerm collapsed a leaf `Invalid` in mod position to a hole, which
  erases the token entirely.
- `^w^ -> Int` — an invalid face is an *Exp*-sorted tile, so it drags the whole type
  out of Typ sort and the arrow vanishes. `(^w^) -> Int` agrees. Precedence can't fix
  this: an invalid hole is atomic, so it never trips the paren check.
- `?:+^w^` — same trap, but a sum has no single protectable operand; the ascription
  itself is lost. So a sum containing an invalid gets parenthesized whole.
- `hint _ test _ end` with a nested `test … end` — during LTR insert, `test` matched
  deep in the backpack and completed `HintedTest`'s own shard instead of expanding a
  nested `Test`. Leading expanders now only match at the top of the stack (as
  ambiguous polymorphs already did), and hints are force-parenthesized.
- `|=>` inside `{}` — `remold` skipped complete kids when parent sorts matched,
  leaving a stale mold whose empty `in_` then broke MakeTerm.
- `(A ... B) ... C`, `T . A -> B` — the parsers order `.`, `->` and `...` differently;
  the printer now parenthesizes defensively on both sides.
- `Invalid(s)` was rewritten to the fixed string `"Invalid"` on the way back to the
  Menhir AST. That runs during shrinking, so shrinking silently turned counterexamples
  into *different programs* — and `"Invalid"` lexes as a constructor, not a face.
- Bare `lab=e` only parses inside `(…)`, so it wraps at binders and at the root while
  tuple fields don't become `((a=1), (b=2))`.
- Module bodies were an unimplemented TODO in the parenthesizer; item payloads are now
  parenthesized and item expressions wrapped so a printed `;` stays a separator.

**`test/Canonicalize.re`** is the new normalizer: it rewrites a generated term into the
shape print+parse produces (`BuiltinFun` → `Var`, `Nat`/`SInt` → `Int`, floats via
their printed form, `DynamicErrorHole` stripped, bare `TupLabel` → singleton tuple,
`f(_)` → `DeferredAp`). Round-trip and cross-parser tests canonicalize both sides and
then compare *strictly*, instead of loosening the equality relation — one place to look
when a print alias shows up, and `Equality` stays honest.

### `Migrate Test_MenhirFuzz PBT to the full-syntax generator`

- Same switch, and it drops its own bespoke equality settings for `Canonicalize`.

### `Migrate Test_ExplainThis PBT to the full-syntax generator`

- No production fix needed — `decide` handled everything. Adds a regression test
  walking every info-map entry of `let 0 = _ in []` and `fun 0 -> []`.

### `Remove the curated AST generators`

- Deletes ~580 lines of hand-written generators and their wrappers.

---

Side effect worth noting: menhir's arbitrarily resolved reduce/reduce conflicts drop
from **52 on `dev` to 5**, and it no longer reports any never-reduced productions
(`dev` has 3). Shift/reduce goes 57 → 69.
